criteria.criterion: `rebar transition <id> <from> closed --force="<reason>"` bypasses the close gate exactly as `--force-close=<reason>` did — verified by a unit test asserting `verify_completion` is never invoked on that path.
A bare `--force` on a close bypasses the gate with the reason `(no reason given)`, matching `rebar claim --force` — verified by a `_parse_flags` unit test.
`--force` on `open -> in_progress` still bypasses the start-work gate — verified by the existing start-work gate tests passing unchanged.
`--force --reason="x"` on `open -> in_progress` still records `x` as the audit note — verified by a unit test asserting the note text.
`--force-close` (with or without a value) exits non-zero with an error message containing `--force` — verified by a unit test; it must not be silently skipped.

The literal flag string `--force-close` survives ONLY in the specified places (frozen corpora, CHANGELOG.md, docs/release-notes.md, parser rejection branch, and its test) — verified by tree-wide grep.
`docs/cli-reference.md` is regenerated so the CI drift gate passes — verified by `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check` exiting 0.
`CHANGELOG.md` records the rename under a breaking-change heading — verified by `grep -q -- '--force-close' CHANGELOG.md` finding the entry.
No force flag is exposed over MCP — verified by `grep -q 'deliberately NO ``force`` bypass' src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` and no `force` field appearing in the MCP transition tool signature.
